questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Unit-elastic point on a demand curve
questions.learningObjective: Identify unit elasticity on a demand curve
questions.stem: Ticket #101: price and quantity both change by five percent at a point; what elasticity holds there?

options.text: Demand is unit elastic because percentage changes in price and quantity match.
Demand is perfectly elastic because any price change wipes out quantity.
options.misconception: overstates responsiveness to a small price change

options.text: Demand is inelastic because quantity responds less than price changes overall.
options.misconception: confuses a five percent match with inelastic response

options.text: Demand is elastic because quantity responds more than price changes here.
options.misconception: treats equal percentages as an elastic response

questions.explanation: Unit elasticity means equal percentage changes in price and quantity. The tempting elastic label ignores the exact equality of the two percentages.
questions.hint: Compare the two percentage changes directly.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Utility maximisation for one good
questions.stem: Ticket #102: utility is U=10q-0.5q^2 and price is 4; find the quantity maximising net benefit.

options.text: The quantity is 5 because marginal utility equals 5 at that point.
options.misconception: stops before equating marginal utility to price

options.text: The quantity is 6 because marginal utility 10-q equals price 4.
The quantity is 10 because total utility peaks at the vertex of the parabola.
options.misconception: confuses total utility peak with net benefit peak

options.text: The quantity is 2 because price divided by slope gives the stopping point.
options.misconception: divides price by slope instead of solving equality

questions.explanation: Set marginal utility 10-q equal to price 4, giving q=6. The vertex of total utility is not the net benefit peak.
questions.hint: Set marginal utility equal to price and solve.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal utility and the chosen quantity
questions.learningObjective: Explain why marginal utility falls at higher quantities
questions.stem: Ticket #103: explain why a consumer buys fewer units as marginal utility declines while price stays fixed.

answer.exemplar: As marginal utility falls below price, each extra unit costs more value than it adds, so the consumer stops buying before that point.

questions.explanation: The consumer stops when marginal utility drops to price. Extra units beyond that point reduce net benefit even though total utility still rises.
questions.hint: Compare marginal utility to price at the margin.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal rate of substitution
questions.learningObjective: Define MRS as a ratio of marginal utilities
questions.stem: Ticket #105: which expression equals the marginal rate of substitution between goods X and Y?

options.text: It equals total utility of X over total utility of Y at the bundle.
options.misconception: uses total instead of marginal utility

options.text: It equals MUy divided by MUx, reversing the goods in the ratio.
It equals price of X divided by price of Y only, ignoring utilities.
options.misconception: confuses MRS with the price ratio

options.text: It equals MUx divided by MUy, the rate at which X trades for Y.

questions.explanation: MRS is MUx/MUy. Reversing gives the inverse trade rate; price ratio is a market condition, not the preference trade rate.
questions.hint: MRS compares marginal utilities, not prices or totals.

questions.stem: Ticket #106: willingness to pay is 12 and price is 7; what is consumer surplus on that unit?

questions.hint: Subtract price from willingness to pay.

questions.learningObjective: Locate unit elasticity on a linear demand
questions.stem: Ticket #108: on a linear demand, at which quantity is demand unit elastic? Stage one: midpoint. Stage two: confirm elasticity equals one there.

options.text: At half the midpoint quantity, where elasticity equals two.
At the price-axis intercept, where elasticity is zero.
options.misconception: places unit elasticity at the intercept

options.text: At the quantity-axis intercept, where elasticity is infinite.
options.misconception: places unit elasticity at the other intercept

options.text: At the midpoint of the demand curve, where elasticity equals one.

questions.explanation: Linear demand has unit elasticity at its midpoint. Intercepts have extreme elasticities, not one.
questions.hint: Recall the midpoint property of linear demand.

options.text: q=10 because MU is highest at the first unit only.
options.misconception: stops at first unit with highest MU

options.text: q=6 because MU just equals 4 at that row of the table.
q=2 because price divided by MU gives the stop point.
q=8 because MU exceeds price for many units.
options.misconception: keeps buying while MU above price

questions.explanation: Buy while MU exceeds price; stop when MU reaches price. The table row with MU=4 gives q=6.

questions.topic: Marginal utility and the chosen quantity
questions.learningObjective: Predict effect of a price fall on quantity
questions.stem: Ticket #110: if price falls, at what quantity does marginal utility now equal the new price?

options.text: At the same quantity, because preferences do not change.
At a lower quantity, because cheaper goods are bought less.
At a higher quantity, because lower price needs lower MU to match.
At zero, because free goods have no marginal value.
options.misconception: confuses free goods with priced goods

questions.explanation: A lower price matches marginal utility at a larger quantity. Preferences unchanged but the equality point shifts.
questions.hint: Lower price matches lower marginal utility at higher q.

questions.learningObjective: State the equalisation rule across goods
questions.stem: Ticket #111: state the rule that equalises marginal utility per dollar across all purchased goods.

answer.exemplar: Spend so that marginal utility per dollar is equal for every good purchased, otherwise reallocate to the higher ratio.

questions.explanation: Equal MU per dollar maximises total utility. If ratios differ, shifting money to the higher ratio raises utility.
questions.hint: Equalise the ratios at the optimum.

MRS equals Px/Py, the price ratio of the two goods.

questions.explanation: Tangency requires MRS equal to the price ratio. Reversing gives the wrong trade rate.
questions.hint: Set MRS equal to Px over Py.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Consumer surplus from willingness to pay
questions.learningObjective: Compute surplus for a marginal buyer
questions.stem: Ticket #148: the marginal buyer has WTP equal to price; their consumer surplus is?

options.text: Price, because surplus equals price paid.
Zero, because WTP minus price equals zero.
WTP, because surplus equals willingness to pay.
Infinity, because marginal buyers are unlimited.

questions.explanation: Surplus is WTP minus price; equality gives zero. Price or WTP alone is not surplus.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Consumer surplus from a linear demand
questions.stem: Ticket #149: demand intercept price 20, quantity 8 at zero price; surplus triangle?
questions.explanation: At zero price surplus is whole triangle 0.5*8*20=80. Using rectangle would be 160.
questions.hint: Area under demand to price axis.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Unit-elastic point on a demand curve
questions.stem: Ticket #150: unit elasticity requires percentage change in quantity to?

options.text: Be less than percentage change in price.
Exceed percentage change in price.
Equal percentage change in price.
Be zero regardless of price change.

questions.explanation: Unit elasticity means equal percentage responses. Exceeding or lagging gives elastic or inelastic.

questions.topic: Utility maximisation for one good
questions.stem: Ticket #151: U=30q-3q^2; marginal utility at q=4?
questions.explanation: Derivative 30-6q at q=4 is 6. Total utility at q=4 is 72, not marginal.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal utility and the chosen quantity
questions.stem: Ticket #152: a price increase reduces chosen quantity because?

options.text: Higher price makes the good free, increasing quantity.
Higher price lowers marginal utility directly.
Higher price raises total utility, reducing need.
Higher price requires higher marginal utility, reached at lower q.

questions.explanation: Higher price matches marginal utility at a smaller quantity. Price does not change utility function.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal utility per dollar
questions.stem: Ticket #153: optimality condition for two goods is?

options.text: MUx = MUy.
MUx/Px = MUy/Py.
Px = Py.
MUx*Px = MUy*Py.

questions.explanation: Equal MU per dollar is MUx/Px=MUy/Py. Equal MUs or prices are special cases.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal rate of substitution
questions.stem: Ticket #154: explain the tangency condition for consumer equilibrium.

answer.exemplar: At equilibrium the indifference curve is tangent to the budget line, so MRS equals the price ratio.

questions.explanation: Tangency equates MRS to price ratio. Crossing would allow utility gains.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Consumer surplus from willingness to pay
questions.stem: Ticket #155: WTPs 8,6,4 and price 3; total surplus?

options.text: Surplus is 3 because only lowest buyer counts.
Surplus is 18 because sum WTPs 18 minus price 3.
Surplus is 9 because 5+3+1=9.
Surplus is 0 because price below all WTP? no.

questions.explanation: Sum (WTP-price): 5+3+1=9. Subtracting price once from total WTP is wrong.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Consumer surplus from a linear demand
questions.stem: Ticket #156: demand Q=10-P; price falls from 4 to 2; surplus change?

options.text: Surplus becomes 0 because price low.
Surplus falls from 32 to 18, a decrease of 14.
Surplus unchanged at 18 because intercept same.
Surplus rises from 18 to 32, an increase of 14.

questions.explanation: At P=4, Q=6, surplus=0.5*6*6=18. At P=2, Q=8, surplus=0.5*8*8=32. Increase 14.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Unit-elastic point on a demand curve
questions.stem: Ticket #157: explain what unit elasticity means for a demand curve.

answer.exemplar: Unit elasticity means a one percent price change produces an equal one percent quantity change, so revenue stays constant.

questions.explanation: Equal percentage responses define unit elasticity. Revenue is unchanged at that point.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Marginal utility and the chosen quantity
questions.stem: Ticket #159: marginal utility is the change in total utility from?

options.text: All units consumed divided by quantity.
One more unit consumed.
Price times quantity.
Income divided by price.

questions.explanation: Marginal utility is the increment from one more unit. Average utility divides total by quantity.
